Rafael,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, StellarFleet is excited to move forward but Legal asked me to put a few firm asks in writing so we can get a single redline back-and-forth. Our main constraints:

- Maintenance windows: cannot have more than 3 maintenance days per year that can impact production availability; we'd like a 72-hour advance notice for any maintenance that may affect the SLA.
- Service credits: StellarFleet requires a minimum credit of 10% for any monthly availability below 99.5% and an escalating credit ladder for lower tiers.
- Response times: Priority 1 incident — 30 minute acknowledgement and 4 hour remediation target in the order form.

Attached is our internal suggested markup to the SLA (stellarfleet_sla_redline_v3.docx). Can you run this by Redwood Legal and Ops and let me know which items are negotiable vs. company policy?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are aiming for signature by mid-December.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: MSA discussion — initial SLA redlines

Elena — thanks for sending the redlines and for outlining priorities. I reviewed the doc and pulled Ops + Legal in on this thread so we can be direct about constraints. High-level reactions:

- Maintenance cadence: We can commit to a maximum of 6 maintenance days per year if StellarFleet takes advantage of our off-peak scheduling (we typically run larger maintenance during region-specific low-traffic windows). We can scope to a shared maintenance calendar to minimize surprises.
- Notice: 72-hour notice is reasonable for planned maintenance that is non-customer-impacting. For maintenance that could affect the SLA we typically request 7 days to coordinate fallbacks; 72 hours is aggressive but not impossible for minor changes.
- Credits: Our standard service credit matrix starts at 99.0% -> 5% credit. Escalating credits at lower tiers are negotiable but we need to cap aggregate monthly credits to protect capacity.
- P1 response: 30 minute acknowledgement is fine; remediation targets vary by incident class and root cause (platform vs. customer config). We can accept a 4-hour remediation aim for Redwood-caused incidents; we propose an exception clause for third-party cloud outages.

I've attached a working PDF of our proposed counter-redline (redwood-msasla-v5_redline.pdf) with inline comments. Counsel (lauren) — can you review the notice/credits language and propose wording that preserves Redwood's fallbacks but addresses StellarFleet's operating needs?

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal to agree to a single-track redline and return by 11/26.
2) Ops to sign off on maintenance cadence and notice windows by 11/27.
3) Commercial to prepare an updated order form for signature and draft DocuSign link by 12/03.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute sync tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks — Rafael

--

Elena, Rafael — quick legal read here. I annotated Redwood's PDF and included rationale inline:

- Maintenance notice: we can accept 72-hour notice for low-impact activities; for any activity that reduces capacity or triggers the SLA, the operative notice should be 7 days. I'll propose language that distinguishes "planned non-impact maintenance" from "planned SLA-impacting maintenance."
- Credit ladder: counterproposal attached: a three-tier ladder starting at 99.0% (5%), 98.0% (10%), <98.0% (15%) with an aggregate monthly cap at 25% invoice credit. The cap mitigates the risk of cascading credits for systemic issues while still providing meaningful remedy.
- Third-party outages: we will explicitly carve out public cloud provider incidents and force majeure, with a clear remediation attribution process (post-incident RCA to validate credit eligibility).

I will aim to produce a single redline bundle (MSA + Order Form consolidated) and deliver to the thread by EOD 11/26. Rafael — would like Ops (aditya) to confirm the 6-day/year maintenance cap vs. 3-day ask and whether we can commit to a shared calendar entry for StellarFleet.

Lauren Bishop

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Quick ops confirmation:

- Maintenance frequency: Ops can operationally support a limit of 4 customer-facing maintenance days per year for the StellarFleet tenant if we agree to a firm shared calendar and a defined blackout period (we cannot schedule more than one customer-impacting maintenance per quarter for high-impact changes). Policy-wise, engineering reserves the right to schedule emergency patches as needed (we'll flag these and provide post-event RCA).
- Notice: we will commit to a 7-day notice for SLA-impacting maintenance; 72-hours for non-SLA-impacting items is OK.
- Response targets: P1 acknowledgement <= 30 mins; remediation target of 6 hours for complex infrastructure fixes, 4 hours when the cause is in Redwood control.

If StellarFleet is firm on 3 maintenance days/year, we need that in the order form as an exception and require a higher committed spend to prioritize their change windows.

Aditya Rao

Thanks everyone for the quick reviews and for being explicit about constraints — this helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from our side after reviewing lauren's attached counter:

- StellarFleet can accept 4 customer-impacting maintenance days/year (we had internal pressure for 3, but 4 is workable if tied to a shared calendar and a no-more-than-one-per-quarter rule).
- We accept the 7-day notice for SLA-impacting maintenance and 72-hours for other items.
- On credits: the three-tier ladder is reasonable; our procurement team would like the aggregate cap to be 30% rather than 25% given the criticality of the workload. Would Redwood consider 30% cap if StellarFleet agrees to a minimum 12-month committed usage (order form spend to be defined)?

If you can share a consolidated MSA+Order Form redline with those two conditional items (4 maintenance days + 30% cap tied to 12-month commitment) by EOD Wednesday 12/02, I'll get procurement to validate and we can route to signature. Also please include a DocuSign stub in the order form so procurement can run an internal approval path.

Elena
